chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn Fuzayl, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)

Regarding the man who marries the woman upon a stipulation that she is a virgin, so he finds her as having been married before. Is it allowed for him that he resides with her? He (peace be upon him) said: 'The virginity can be torn from the riding and from the jumping.'

key_terms.الْمَرْكَبُ: Riding (metaphor for non-coital loss of virginity)
key_terms.ثَيِّبٌ: Non-virgin woman (previously married or sexually active)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling if a man marries a woman believing she is a virgin but finds she is not?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the stipulation of virginity in marriage is not limited to physical hymenal integrity but includes sexual inexperience, as the term 'bikr' can refer to one who has not yet engaged in intercourse (jumpa) or riding (nazwa). This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that marital validity depends on the substantive reality of the condition rather than a rigid physical marker, allowing the husband to remain with the wife even if the physical sign is absent. This interpretation aligns with the broader Islamic legal understanding that 'virginity' encompasses both physical and experiential states, preventing unjust annulment based on technicalities.
